verdict.rationale: Convex documents its own approach to per-user access control: every public request can be checked against authorization rules written in code inside server functions, together with built-in auth (Convex Auth, Clerk/Auth0/WorkOS, OIDC). It explicitly says it does not need an RLS-style framework, so there is no declarative row-level policy or security-rules layer, and developers write the checks themselves. Missing for 10: a declarative RLS/security-rules mechanism, documented per-row or per-user policy examples, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
